blocks.text: The chapter first hears a precise number—144,000 sealed from the tribes of Israel—and then sees an unnumbered multitude from every nation standing before the throne and the Lamb. The 144,000 later appear with the Lamb, but readers differ over how this numbered group relates to the great multitude: whether the visions describe the same people in different imagery or distinct groups remains disputed.

Across Revelation, imagery repeatedly reworks Israel’s Scriptures, and its visions unfold through major sevenfold sequences of seals, trumpets, and bowls, with pauses and recurring motifs. This wider pattern provides the setting in which Revelation 7 appears as an interlude within the book’s larger sequence of visions.
